subject: Re: Data retention exception for Acme Corp - logging controls & PII
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-corp.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Sabrina Ortiz <sabrina.ortiz@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Data retention requirements & exception request

Hi Neha / Sabrina,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — helpful to see Redwood's routing and caching approach. As discussed on the call, our security team needs a data retention exception for the POC: we cannot retain any PII-containing request/response payloads beyond the session (effectively 0-retention for PII). We can tolerate short-term non-PII logs for troubleshooting (<=7 days) but PII must either be redacted in-line or not logged at all.

Specific asks from Acme security:
- 0-retention for PII in request/response bodies (no persisted copies)
- Audit logs for admin actions can be retained up to 90 days, but must exclude PII
- Proof of technical controls: redaction/tokenization flow, KMS key usage, and logging config examples

I've attached our retention request PDF that lists required controls and a sample questionnaire. Can Redwood support this for the POC? If not fully, please outline the gaps and any trade-offs.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Security, Acme Corp
[jordan.lee@acme-corp.com]
Attachment: acme-retention-request.pdf

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-21T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Data retention exception for Acme - need ops/security signoff

Marissa / Rafael — forwarding Acme's ask (thread below). POC request is pretty strict: 0-retention for PII in request/response bodies, <=7 days for non-PII logs, 90 days for admin/audit logs (PII excluded).

Can you confirm feasibility and list any blockers or configuration changes we'll need? Specific questions:
- Can our hosted runtime be configured to not persist request/response payloads that contain fields flagged as PII? If not, what work is required (engineering/ops time)?
- Alternatives: on-the-fly redaction via schema + masking, or client-side preprocessing (they prefer server-side).
- Impact on observability/troubleshooting: what visibility will ops have if PII is stripped? Any recommended short-term offsets?
- Compliance evidence we can provide (KMS key rotation info, audit trail snippets, SOC2 extracts).

Acme indicated this will cover a 6-week POC. They will probably want the exception written into the mutual action plan and attached to the SOW if we agree. I'm copying Jordan on the follow-up once we have a proposal.

HubSpot: https://hubspot.example/contacts/ACME-12345
Thanks — Neha

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-corp.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Data retention exception for Acme Corp - proposed approach

Hi Jordan / Neha,

Thanks for the patience while Rafael and I reviewed the request. Short version: we can support Acme's POC with the retention controls you described by combining runtime redaction and a scoped retention exception. Below is the proposed configuration and next steps.

Proposed configuration:
- PII handling: implement runtime request/response field-level redaction for fields you flag as PII. Redacted values are replaced with one-way hashes (no reversible token) and the raw payload is not persisted to disk or long-term storage. This achieves the effective 0-retention semantics for PII.
- Non-PII logs: keep application and infra logs (no PII fields) for 7 days for troubleshooting. Access is limited to named ops engineers via RBAC.
- Audit/admin logs: retain up to 90 days, scrubbed for PII, exported only to your S3 or audit store if requested.

Technical notes and trade-offs:
- Observability: with field-level redaction, we maintain request-level metadata (request id, model variant, latency, error codes) so triage is still possible, but payload-level debugging will be limited. We recommend a short feature flag that enables temporary payload capture for a single session under strict access controls if needed during debugging.
- Implementation effort: we can enable runtime redaction via our config layer and a lightweight mapping file for PII field names. Rafael estimates ~5 engineering days for validation and automated tests (can be done in our hosted environment under a feature-flagged release).
- Evidence: attaching a short SOC2 extract and a refined proposal document. We can also provide KMS usage notes and sample audit snippets.

Next steps:
1) Jordan: confirm the list of fields you consider PII (we'll use that to build the mapping).
2) If accepted, we'll produce a short retention exception addendum (1-2 pages) to attach to the SOW and route for signatures (DocuSign link below).
3) Rafael and I will schedule a 60-minute technical kickoff with your security and platform teams to validate the mapping and run a short test.

Timeline: we can deliver the validation + test environment in ~3 weeks from field list confirmation.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/containers/ABC-RETENTION-2026
Attachments: redwood-data-retention-proposal-v2.pdf, SOC2-audit-extract.pdf
